text: Hogwarts Loop 是面向 DeepSeek Harness Web 的多代理工作流插件：它注册 hogwarts-loop 技能和 hogwarts_dispatch 工具，为大型工程任务规划检查点，并按角色派发实现与独立评审。主要能力包括复用会话内角色子代理、为角色配置模型路由、在设置页编辑派发参数，以及通过分步审查推进工程任务。适合需要跨文件实施与评审的开发工作；需使用 Harness profile 和 Node.js 20 以上环境。

Hogwarts Loop is a DeepSeek Harness plugin for large engineering tasks. Its skill plans checkpoints; hogwarts_dispatch starts or continues role-based agents for implementation and review. Configure role models and dispatch settings in the UI. Requires a Harness profile and Node.js 20+.
想把大型开发任务拆成多个检查点，逐步实现并评审。
让主代理规划任务，再把实现工作交给固定角色的子代理。
我希望不同职责的子代理使用各自配置的模型。
需要在同一会话里继续使用之前创建的角色代理。
有没有能给 DSH 配置子代理模型和派发参数的设置界面？
想让代码先由一个代理实现，再由另一个代理独立检查。
How can I split a large engineering task into planned checkpoints with implementation and review?
I need persistent role-based subagents with configurable model routes in a Harness session.
Hogwarts Loop 的功能「角色子代理派发」：通过 hogwarts_dispatch 按角色启动或继续一个子代理，并返回 started 或 continued 状态及子代理标识。
Hogwarts Loop 的功能「分步工程循环」：hogwarts-loop 技能引导主代理规划检查点、派发实现任务并组织独立评审，适合较大的工程改动。
Hogwarts Loop 的功能「按角色配置模型」：配置结构为不同角色保存 provider、model 等路由参数，派发器据角色设置创建子代理。
Hogwarts Loop 的功能「角色设置页」：在 Settings 面板和插件行配置入口注册同一表单，供用户编辑角色与派发设置。

**Plan → build → review → commit, as a [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/harness/) plugin.** One subagent per cast member, each dispatched on **its own configurable model**.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · dsh-hogwarts-loop：[`@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop) packages the `hogwarts-loop` discipline: take a large engineering effort from a plan to reviewed, committed code in small, independently verified checkpoints. The methodology ships as a skill, every cast member is a managed subagent started through one tool, and the model behind each role is set in the client instead of being baked into the prompt.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · What it adds：| Capability | Form | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The loop methodology and each role's detailed duties | the `hogwarts-loop` skill (also triggerable as `/hogwarts-loop`) | `skill/SKILL.md`, `skill/references/*.md` |
| Finding record, batch validation, convergence cap, and evaluation guide | markdown contract + synthetic and repository-derived cases | `skill/references/review-contract.md`, `skill/references/evaluation.md`, `skill/assets/eval-*.md` |
| Create or continue the same cast member within a parent session | the `hogwarts_dispatch` tool | registered by `index.js` |
| Edit provider / model / effort / output cap per role | **Settings → Hogwarts Loop**, plus the Plugins page row for this plugin | `client.js` (browser half) |

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · What it adds：**One parent session, one child per role.** Checkpoints and fix rounds keep the same `childId`; changing `description`, completing a CP, or becoming inactive does not create a new Harry. Each role is independent, so Harry and Severus retain separate histories. Dispatch is nonblocking: wait for a role's report before assigning its next CP; concurrent calls to that role do not create parallel workers.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · What it adds：Bindings survive plugin reload and resuming the same parent session. A continuation failure never silently creates a replacement. Older histories with ambiguous role bindings require intervention instead of guessing. A genuinely new parent session starts its own cast, rehydrated from the plan.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · What it adds：Results distinguish `started` from `continued`. Creation reports the configured provider/model; continuation identifies the existing child rather than claiming it uses newly edited defaults. `cwd` is creation-only: a non-empty `cwd` on a later call is rejected. Omit it to preserve the child's established working directory. The roster label keeps the first `description`; later briefs do not relabel the child.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Conditional ablation：The skill requires a complexity report on every Harry delivery. When the
[ablation policy](skill/references/ablation.md) triggers, Harry runs controlled
removal/substitution experiments without weakening acceptance, verifies the
combined survivor, and gives Severus the evidence to audit. This is a workflow
gate, not a runtime code-size scanner; direct manual dispatch skips the skill's
checkpoint discipline. Thresholds and counting rules have one canonical home.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Review discipline：The [review contract](skill/references/review-contract.md) keeps a few rules:
validate blocking candidates before repair, preserve evidence and finding IDs,
and independently check the fix rather than repeating the whole review.
Complete repair/re-review rounds and evidence-only batches have separate budgets;
normal proof gathering is not counted as another repair round. Eligible same-root
advisor-guided diagnosis or implementation has a narrow precedence rule, without
a code-edit prerequisite; it is not a budget reset or exemption for blind probe
churn or unrelated work (see Escalation below).

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Review discipline：[Evaluation](skill/references/evaluation.md) distinguishes fixture checks from real
before/after review comparisons. A [repository-derived pair and repair replay](skill/assets/eval-legacy-inputs.md)
complements the synthetic cases; [scoring and provenance](skill/assets/eval-legacy-expectations.md)
stay outside reviewer context. None of these artifacts is a model-quality score.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Review discipline：Working plans, progress lists and review reports stay in the session or task-scoped
temporary storage by default, not in Git or behind `.gitignore`. Only an explicitly
approved, maintained roadmap/design document is durable; the shipped plan template
is a product asset, not a filled-in execution report.
@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Install：Requires Node.js ≥ 20 and a DeepSeek Harness profile.
@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · From the Add plugin wizard：Type `@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop` into the **Add plugin** wizard's search box and click **Install**.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · With the `dsh` CLI：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop
dsh web
```

No build step and no restart, but see the reload note below.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Use it：The plugin is not a task and has no start button. Once installed it is always present, providing three things: the `hogwarts_dispatch` tool, the `hogwarts-loop` skill, and the settings page. "Making it work" means triggering the skill, which in turn directs the main agent to dispatch. The plugin stays loaded even when nobody triggers it.

Three ways in:

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Configure the cast：**Settings → Hogwarts Loop** (the settings entry at the bottom of the sidebar) is the main entry. It registers as a `settings.section` with order 60.

The same form has a second entry point: **Plugins → Installed plugins → `@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop` → the `hogwarts-loop` row → Configure** (`plugins.row.config`).

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Configure the cast：The page lists every cast member, one row each: **provider** and **model** are dropdowns fed by the host's model catalog (`remote.session.modelCatalog()`, grouped per provider); switching the provider switches the model to that provider's first entry. **Reasoning effort** is a dropdown built from the levels the selected model actually supports (blank = the model default), and the **max output tokens** field may be left empty. Below them, **Dispatch settings** holds the subagent backend and the delegation depth cap.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Configure the cast：Save writes every change as a single atomic, version-fenced `mutate` to this plugin's row in the current profile. **The next newly created role uses it** — no reinstall and no restart. Continuing an existing role preserves its child session and does not apply new creation defaults or replace it to switch models.

Defaults (the behaviour when nothing is overridden):

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Configure the cast：| Role | Seat | Default model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `harry` | implementer (writes the code, runs the gates) | `deepseek-flash` |
| `severus` | reviewer (correctness lead; read-only) | `deepseek-v4-pro` |
| `alastor` | security specialist | `deepseek-v4-pro` |
| `filius` | performance specialist | `deepseek-flash` |
| `minerva` | concurrency specialist | `deepseek-flash` |
| `argus` | closeout UI walkthrough | `deepseek-flash` |
| `voldemort` | one-problem escalation advisor (read-only) | `deepseek-v4-pro` |

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Escalation: Voldemort：Harry makes **three independent attempts on the same unresolved problem**: each needs a substantive approach, implementation and validation evidence. “Same-root” tracks stable failure and acceptance criteria, with a proven root or unproven hypotheses; exact root proof is not required, and changing diagnostic hypotheses does not reset attempts. A red gate can end a failed attempt before review; confirmed same-root P1 or P2 failures after implementation also qualify. Repeated commands, progress messages, evidence-only probes and different roots do not count. If attempt three succeeds, do not escalate. Otherwise **Harry promptly reports all three approaches and exact failure evidence to Albus**, rather than retrying independently.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Escalation: Voldemort：Albus brings in `voldemort` as a **read-only one-problem escalation advisor**, with the spec/acceptance, changes and failures from each attempt, ruled-out causes and current hypothesis. Voldemort thinks, diagnoses and provides executable next steps, hypotheses and bounded acceptance signals; he never edits code, runs builds/tests, commits, self-closes a fix or takes other checkpoints. Albus relays advice to **the same Harry child**, who always implements/tests, then relays actual results and failure reports back so Voldemort can adjust. Severus independently closes the fix.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Escalation: Voldemort：Continue until solved with **no fixed collaboration-round or total-attempt cap**. Preserve the first three attempts and cumulative history. Albus reassesses every round and arranges bounded diagnosis **or** implementation: an evidence-driven new/revised hypothesis or diagnostic question, named commands, time/scenario limits and decidable signals. Diagnosis requires no code edits; Harry executes and reports actual results to the read-only advisor through Albus, and evidence must be validated before authorizing repair. The [review contract](skill/references/review-contract.md) lets such work on this already eligible problem exceed cumulative repair/evidence counts, including diagnostic-only rounds, without recurring human-extension requests. Unescalated checkpoints and unrelated problems retain ordinary budgets; blind probe churn is not licensed. Never hide unlimited retries or blindly repeat ineffective work. Scope and mandatory approvals remain; honor human stops and report real permission, environment or external-prerequisite blockers honestly.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Escalation: Voldemort：**Guidance ends at independent problem closure, not checkpoint completion.** Albus records the scoped evidence/exit and stops advisor dispatches; Harry continues independently. The same advisor child keeps memory but no standing task. A different problem needs its own three failures and fresh Albus scope/exit brief. [Problem-scoped advisor lifecycle](skill/references/review-contract.md#problem-scoped-advisor-lifecycle) defines target verification and unrelated-red attribution: local closure is not checkpoint APPROVE or permission to commit a red checkpoint.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Escalation: Voldemort：The *Escalation* section of [skill/SKILL.md](skill/SKILL.md) is the workflow rule; `DEFAULT_ROLES` in [index.js](index.js) defines the cast. These are **agent work contracts, not runtime ACLs or automatic counters**. Harry/Voldemort continuations prepend the current persona, including for historical children, without replacing the child or its creation-time model. Frozen old personas remain for identity matching only.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Escalation: Voldemort：> The form writes this plugin's **profile row** (the `hogwarts-loop` entry in `cordis.patch.yml`). Editing that row's `config` by hand or in bulk works too; the field definitions are the `Config` export in `index.js`.

**Albus is you** — the main session. Its model is chosen by the session's model picker and is not controlled by this plugin; the plugin only decides the route of every subagent it dispatches.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Why the form looks like this：- The form registers twice — in the settings panel's `settings.section` and in the Plugins page's `plugins.row.config` (key `@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop#hogwarts-loop`) — and both render the same `FormBody`.
- The settings-panel entry resolves this plugin's namespace through the shared `settings.describe` mirror (matching the `hogwarts-loop` suffix, so an `include:` prefix still works) and then gets a version-fenced write handle via `ctx.configForms.get(ns)`. The Plugins entry receives the bound `form` directly from the page, so it never has to guess a namespace.
- On the host side, `Config` marks the two top-level objects `delegation` and `roles` as `.volatile()` (schemastery cannot nest volatile, so the reference has to sit on the object). That is both what makes the settings service treat the entry as editable and serve the settings panel, and what guarantees new role creation reads the **current** defaults rather than a snapshot taken when the plugin activated.
- When the model catalog cannot be read (expired login, failed catalog request), the same fields fall back to text inputs instead of breaking the page.

text: @dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Verify the routing：Expect `agentModel` / `config.model` to equal that role's configured model.

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Repository layout：```
.
├── package.json              # @dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop; dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client
├── cordis.patch.yml          # inserts the hogwarts-loop row
├── index.js                  # host half: Config schema, skill registration, hogwarts_dispatch

@dyikai/dsh-hogwarts-loop README · Known limits：- The settings entry is a **page the plugin registers itself** (`settings.section`), not a form the host auto-generates from `Config` — that renderer does not exist in this client version yet (`autoGenerate` is not consumed by any built-in client).
- The first dispatch uses a continuable `spawn` backend; later dispatches resume that child. One-shot backends cannot satisfy the persistent-role contract. `fork`-style backends inherit the parent's route and cannot provide independent per-role model selection.
- `delegation.maxDepth` defaults to `1`: a child cannot dispatch further down.
- Children join the parent session's current agent preset and use its tools.
- The plugin is **profile-level**: install it once and every session in this profile sees `hogwarts_dispatch` and the `hogwarts-loop` skill.
